rounds.text: Shree Pushkar Chemicals & Fertilizers Ltd is significantly undervalued by the market, trading at a modest P/E of 18.5 alongside a rules-based screen score of 95 out of 100 pointing to high-confidence buy territory [E1, E61]. The business demonstrates robust compound growth, delivering 22% sales growth and 25% profit growth over the trailing twelve months, which is supported by a strong sector tailwind score of +0.52 [E16, E19, E68]. Operating momentum is accelerating, evidenced by quarterly operating margins expanding to 12% in September 2026 and a positive institutional money flow change of +0.36 percentage points [E29, E42]. Management provides clear visibility toward at least INR 1,250 crores in total sales with three-digit profitability for the year, backed by ongoing strategic expansions such as the new chemical plant at Unit 5 and a consolidated solar capacity increase to 20.6 megawatts [E72, E78, E84]. Furthermore, intrinsic value models indicate a vast margin of safety at 54.8%, while the reverse DCF reveals that today's price assumes a meager 7.1% earnings growth against a historical baseline of 18.0% [E44, E45]. Conceded: free cash flow was negative at Rs -14 Cr in March 2026, borrowings rose to Rs 232 Cr by September 2026, and foreign and domestic institutional holdings have declined since December 2023 [E34, E37, E40, E41].

Shree Pushkar Chemicals & Fertilizers Ltd carries a significant structural vulnerability in its cash generation profile, evidenced by a negative free cash flow of Rs -14 Cr in March 2026 despite reported profits [E34]. This cash drain coincides with a sharp escalation in borrowings, which surged to Rs 232 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 131 Cr a year earlier [E37], alongside a current ratio that provides only an adequate but thin buffer at 1.68x [E36]. Furthermore, the valuation is heavily exposed to temporary external tailwinds rather than enduring fundamental strength, as management explicitly admitted that current pricing spikes in key products like H-Acid are unsustainable and represent short-lived volatility lasting only weeks or months rather than the long term [E89]. Institutional confidence is also visibly retreating, with foreign institutional holding dropping from 1.35% in December 2023 to 0.58% in September 2026 [E40], and domestic institutional holding similarly declining from 0.75% to 0.28% over the same period [E41]. Conceded: the company trades at a modest P/E of 18.5x [E1] and management has provided optimistic sales visibility targeting up to INR 2,000 crores by 2027-2028 [E73]. However, historical data reveals severe volatility, highlighted by a staggering worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -81.8% [E51], while recent margin expansion sits on an inconsistent yearly trend over the last two years [E30] and a low three-year median return on equity of just 11% [E26].

Conceded: free cash flow was negative at Rs -14 Cr in March 2026 [E34]. However, this cash deployment directly reflects active, high-conviction reinvestment into ongoing growth projects like the advanced-stage Units 5 and 6 at Ratnagiri [E80] and a major INR 70 crore capex approved for Unit 5 [E78], all fully backed by robust internal accruals totaling INR 92 crores [E79]. The surge in borrowings to Rs 232 Cr [E37] supports this aggressive capacity expansion, matched by a comfortable liquidity buffer of non-lien deposits amounting to Rs 125 crores [E88]. While the bear points to retreating institutional holdings [E40, E41], the overall institutional money flow is flagged as POSITIVE MONEY FLOW with an aggregate holding change of +0.36 percentage points, accompanied by an increase in promoter backing to 69.45% alongside a INR 45 crore warrant infusion [E39, E42, E87]. Although management notes certain pricing spikes are short-term [E89], the broader margin expansion is firmly anchored in structural tailwinds from Chinese environmental and safety compliance shortages [E75], driving stellar financial delivery including a 96.1% year-on-year surge in Q2 FY27 PAT [E81] and robust multi-year sales growth of 22% [E14]. Conceded: the historical peak-to-trough drawdown reached -81.8% [E51] and three-year median ROE stands at 11% [E26], but the company currently boasts a top-tier relative strength rating of 100 [E49] and a rules-based screen score of 95 out of 100 [E61].

Conceded: Units 5 and 6 at Ratnagiri are at an advanced stage of completion [E80] and promoter holdings increased slightly [E39]. However, pointing to these projects does not erase the reality of negative free cash flow at Rs -14 Cr in March 2026 [E34] and a sharp jump in borrowings to Rs 232 Cr by September 2026, up from Rs 131 Cr a year earlier [E37]. While the bull highlights positive institutional money flow [E42], foreign and domestic institutions have actually trimmed their stakes significantly to 0.58% [E40] and 0.28% [E41] respectively. Although the bull attributes margin expansion to structural tailwinds [E75], management itself explicitly warns that current pricing spikes like those in H-Acid are unsustainable and will not last for the longer term [E89]. Conceded: the rules-based screen score is high [E61], but the company carries a low median ROE of 11% over the last 3 years [E26] and a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -81.8% [E51], highlighting that past operational momentum has frequently failed to protect shareholder capital during downturns.

Conceded: free cash flow was negative at Rs -14 Cr in March 2026 [E34]. However, this cash outflow directly reflects active growth investment as the company has poured INR92 crores into ongoing capex projects funded entirely by internal accruals [E79], while continuing to generate robust operating cash flow of Rs 102 Cr with a strong cash conversion of 1.46x [E33, E32]. Conceded: borrowings rose to Rs 232 Cr by September 2026 [E37], but this moderate leverage sits at a manageable debt-to-equity ratio of 0.35x alongside a comfortable liquidity position [E35, E88]. While institutional holdings in foreign and domestic entities declined [E40, E41], the overall institutional money flow registers as positive with a holding change of +0.36 percentage points [E42], supported by growing promoter confidence as seen in their stake increase to 69.45% [E39] and a substantial INR45 crore warrant infusion [E87]. Management's caution on pricing spikes [E89] addresses temporary volatility rather than the structural margin expansion driven by environmental and safety compliance shortages in China [E75], which has already lifted quarterly operating margins to 12% [E29] and propelled a 96.1% year-on-year surge in Q2 PAT [E81]. Finally, while historical drawdowns exist [E51], the current low historical ROE [E26] is being outpaced by a stellar rules-based screen score of 95 out of 100 [E61] and a 5-year profit growth compound rate of 20% [E17].

The bull’s reliance on capital expenditure to justify negative free cash flow [E34] ignores that this spending has coincided with a significant increase in borrowings from Rs 131 Cr to Rs 232 Cr in just one year [E37]. While the bull cites a manageable debt-to-equity ratio [E35], the rapid escalation of debt suggests that internal accruals are insufficient to fund the company's aggressive expansion plans [E79]. Conceded: the company maintains a comfortable liquidity position [E88]. However, the bull’s optimism regarding institutional money flow [E42] is contradicted by the actual exit of foreign and domestic institutions, which have reduced their holdings by 0.77 and 0.47 percentage points respectively [E40, E41]. Furthermore, the bull dismisses management’s warning on pricing sustainability [E89] as temporary, yet the company explicitly admits that current margins are bolstered by unsustainable price spikes in products like H-Acid [E89]. Finally, the bull highlights a 96.1% surge in Q2 PAT [E81], but fails to reconcile this with the company's own admission that fertilizer demand is subdued [E76] and global demand remains weak [E77], creating a precarious reliance on volatile chemical pricing [E89].

evidence.quote: In my opinion, if you ask me, we should be able to achieve at least INR1,250 crores of total sales and profitability should be in three digits.

evidence.fact: Management indicated that revenue for the next year should be around INR2,000 crores, subject to a 10% variation.
evidence.quote: Sir, if I talk about next year, like 2027-2028, in my opinion, we should be somewhere closer to near around INR2,000 crores.

evidence.fact: Management expects turnover to reach close to Rs. 1,250 crores with PAT levels near 9% for FY27, potentially moving toward Rs. 1,350 crores or Rs. 1,400 crores.
evidence.quote: And the kind of visibility I gave in my last concall that in this particular financial year, the company would be achieving close to Rs. 1,250 crores turnover with the PAT levels of around near to the 9% or so. I feel it is quite feasible to achieve these targets, maybe we can have something better than this.

evidence.fact: Management stated that the chemical business margins improved due to strong demand from China resulting from environmental and safety compliance shortages.
evidence.quote: First of all, as far as the chemical space is concerned, the margins have improved mainly because of the China factor. In China, there is a huge shortage going on in terms of dye intermediates, mainly because of various compliances in terms of environment and safety norms in China.

evidence.fact: Management expects quarter three for fertilizers to remain a bit subdued due to the poor season.
evidence.quote: And going forward, I see that quarter three, mainly because of a poor season in terms of fertilizers, it may remain a bit subdued.

evidence.fact: Management noted that global demand is still a bit weak.
evidence.quote: Although we have started the plant, but overall, if you see, global demand is still a bit weak.

evidence.fact: The board approved a capital expenditure of INR70 crores for establishing a new chemical plant at Unit 5, Lote Parshuram, with an additional capacity of 3,000 metric tons per annum.
evidence.quote: In line with our growth strategy, the board has also approved a capital expenditure of INR70 crores for establishing a new chemical plant at Unit 5, Lote Parshuram, with an additional capacity of 3,000 metric tons per annum.

evidence.fact: As of September 30, the company has invested INR92 crores in ongoing capex projects, totally funded by internal accruals.
evidence.quote: As on date, as on 30th of September, the Company has invested INR92 crores in the ongoing capex project, which has been totally funded by the internal accruals of the company.

evidence.fact: At Ratnagiri, Unit 5 and Unit 6 are at an advanced stage of completion.
evidence.quote: At Ratnagiri, Unit 5 and Unit 6 are at the advanced stage of completion, given the continued volatility in raw material prices and availability.

evidence.fact: Profit after tax for Q2 FY27 increased by 96.1% year-on-year to INR35.7 crores with a PAT margin of 8.9%.
evidence.quote: Profit after tax increased by 96.1% year-on-year to INR35.7 crores with a PAT margin of 8.9%.

evidence.fact: Gross profit for Q2 FY27 stood at INR120 crores with a gross margin of 30%.
evidence.quote: Gross profit stood at INR120 crores, registering a growth of INR42 crores year-on-year, with a gross margin of 30%.

evidence.fact: The company delivered an EBITDA of Rs. 50 Cr with an EBITDA margin of approximately 12.0% for the quarter.
evidence.quote: From a profitability perspective, the Company delivered EBITDA of Rs. 50 Cr with an EBITDA margin of approximately 12.0%, reflecting a growth of 88 YoY.

evidence.fact: Consolidated installed solar capacity increased to 20.6 megawatts on a DC basis with the addition of a 10 megawatt DC solar project at Nanded.
evidence.quote: Additionally, our 10 megawatt DC solar project at Nanded, Maharashtra commenced operations during this quarter. With this addition, the company's total installed solar capacity on a consolidated basis has increased to 20.6 megawatt on a DC basis.

evidence.fact: During Q2 FY27, the chemical business recorded sales volume of 14,368 metric tons and the fertilizer business recorded 79,277 metric tons.
evidence.quote: In terms of sales volume, the chemical business recorded 14,368 metric tons, while the fertilizer business recorded 79,277 metric tons during the quarter.

evidence.fact: The fertilizer business recorded a sales volume of 66,527 metric tons while chemical business volumes were 9,113 metric tons in Q1 FY27.
evidence.quote: The fertilizer business recorded the sales volume of 66,527 metric tons compared to 76,288 metric tons in Q1 FY26, while volumes in the chemical business were 9,113 metric tons compared to 14,837 metric tons in the corresponding period.

evidence.fact: The board approved the issuance of 8,54,060 fully convertible warrants to the promoter aggregating up to INR45 crores.
evidence.quote: In this regard, the board has approved the issuance of 8,54,060 fully convertible warrants to Mr. Punit Gopikishan Makharia, Promoter and Chairman and Managing Director of the company, at an issue price of INR526.90 per warrant, aggregating up to INR45 crores.

evidence.fact: The company maintains a comfortable liquidity position with Rs. 125 crores in non-lien deposits as on June 30, 2026.
evidence.quote: From a liquidity perspective, the company continues to maintain a comfortable position with Rs. 125 crores in non-lien deposits as on June 30, 2026.

evidence.fact: Management noted that current pricing spikes in products like H-Acid are not sustainable for the long term.
evidence.quote: And these kinds of unsustainability in terms of pricing and whatever these price hiccups are there as on today's date, these are not going to be forever. So these volatilities could last for a few weeks or few months, but not for a longer term.

evidence.quote: The project is expected to be commissioned by March 2028 and is aimed at catering to the growing demand of our customers.

evidence.quote: So probably we will be getting it before March 2027, the balance.
